get.description:
Returns the authenticated user's live-video broadcasts, or selected owned broadcasts when ids are provided.

At most one of `ids`, `max_results` may be provided. At most one of `ids`, `pagination_token` may be provided.

parameters.name: ids

post.description: Takes one or more of the authenticated user's sources live and returns 201 with the new broadcast. Several sources (`source_id` plus `additional_source_ids`, one per video format) go live together as one broadcast; they must all be RTMP sources in one region, and when one of them is already live its broadcast is returned only if it holds every listed source. The broadcast goes live immediately (state `RUNNING`), even before the encoder sends video, and is ended (`TIMED_OUT`) if no video arrives within 5 minutes. It is announced in a Post unless `should_not_tweet` is true. When the source already has a live broadcast, returns 200 with that broadcast unchanged and ignores the request's `title`, `locale`, `chat_option` and `should_not_tweet`. A missing `tweet_id` means the Post hasn't been created yet, was suppressed with `should_not_tweet`, or could not be created; read it later with GET /2/broadcasts/:id. A 409 `conflict` means the source can't go live right now: either it can't take video before the encoder connects (external HLS sources, or regions where this isn't available), so retry once video is flowing, or another broadcast is live on it, so END that broadcast first. The `detail` says which, and names the live broadcast when known.

Ids are permanent; names can change, so store the id and show the current name. The whole list is returned in one response, without paging.

On a closed or trusted call the session asks the host first (admission: requires_approval).
Ends the authenticated user's media session in the call (its WebSocket receives session.ended with reason left) and removes the user from the call.

get.description:
Retrieves a list of Chat conversations for the authenticated user's inbox, newest first: the most recently active conversation comes first. To find the chat with a particular person, start with participant_query set to their @username or name; with expansions=participant_ids, user.fields=receives_your_chat says how you can message each match. The unread, last_read_event_id and newest_event_id fields give your read state, computed from your latest read receipt and each conversation's latest notifying message. Request them with chat_conversation.fields=unread,last_read_event_id,newest_event_id.

The filters unread_only, type, is_archived, is_muted, participant_ids, participant_query, start_time and end_time are optional, and all filters must match (AND). participant_query keeps conversations where another participant's username, or a word of their display name, starts with the query, ignoring case and accents; with a leading @ it matches usernames only. It considers the 100 people who best match the query, uses only public profile information, and never matches group names, nicknames or messages. start_time and end_time apply to the time of each conversation's latest message.

Each page covers max_results conversations and returns those that match, so a page can hold fewer than max_results, or none, while meta.next_token is set and has_more is true: keep paging, passing meta.next_token as pagination_token. Once a page reaches a conversation whose latest message is older than start_time, has_more is false. A pagination_token only works with the same filters as the request that returned it; with other filters, the request fails with a 400.

When both are provided, `start_time` must be earlier than `end_time`.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: Conversations covered per page (1-1000, default 200). Filtered pages can return fewer.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: meta.next_token from the previous page. Send the same filters with it, or the request fails.

parameters.name: unread_only
parameters.description: Return only unread conversations. A page can be short; keep paging while has_more.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only direct (1:1) or only group conversations. Omit for both.

parameters.name: is_archived
parameters.description: true: only archived; false: only not archived. Omit for both.

parameters.name: is_muted
parameters.description: true: only muted; false: only not muted. Omit for both.

parameters.name: participant_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated numeric user IDs (1-10), all in the chat. Names or @handles: use participant_query.

parameters.name: participant_query
parameters.description: Start here to find someone's chat: their @username or a word of their name (1-50 chars).

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z. Chats whose latest message is at or after this time.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z. Chats whose latest message is before this time.

delete.description: Unarchives a Chat conversation for the authenticated user only. Unarchiving a conversation that is not archived changes nothing. Works for group and 1:1 conversations. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: id

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.

get.description: Retrieves the events of a specific Chat conversation, newest first, with pagination support: messages, key changes, group changes, and read receipts. Events with an id above the conversation's last_read_event_id are unread: they come after the point you read up to. To collect them, page until an event's id is at or below it. Only `id` and `encoded_event` are always present. Events are either end-to-end encrypted or unencrypted, such as messages sent before the conversation was encrypted. Encrypted events carry `conversation_key_version`, and usually `conversation_token` and `message_event_signature`; treat an encrypted event without `message_event_signature` as unverified. An event without `conversation_key_version` is unencrypted. Decode each `encoded_event` client-side, and decrypt it with the conversation key named by `conversation_key_version` when that is present. A page holds up to `max_results` events and can hold fewer while `has_more` is true. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: max_results
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to return.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.

delete.description: Turns off the invite link for an encrypted Chat group conversation. The existing link stops working.

post.summary: Enable a Chat Group Invite Link

The client builds the link and sends it as invite_url, in the form https://x.com/i/chat/group_join/<conversation_id>/<token>, where the token is exactly 10 letters, digits, '-' or '_'. invite_url is required when action_signatures is sent. To make the link expire, send validity_duration_msec or validity_expiry_timestamp_msec. With action_signatures, send validity_expiry_timestamp_msec, because the signed payload carries the expiry. The group name and avatar sent here are stored unencrypted and shown to anyone who opens the link.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the group conversation, starting with `g`.

parameters.name: id

post.summary: Reject Join Requests for a Chat Group Conversation
post.description: Rejects pending requests to join an encrypted Chat group conversation. Only group admins can reject requests. To approve a request instead, add the requesting users with addChatGroupMembers; adding a user clears their pending request.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the group conversation, starting with `g`.

post.description: Adds (initializes or rotates) the encryption keys for a Chat conversation. Call this before sending messages in a new 1:1 conversation, and again with a newer key version to rotate the conversation key. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID as the conversation id; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. The request body must contain the conversation key version and participant keys (the conversation key encrypted for each participant using their public key).

post.description: Adds one or more members to an existing encrypted Chat group conversation, rotating the conversation key. Adding a user who has a pending join request approves that request; approval needs the same key-rotation body as adding any member.

post.description: Removes one or more members from an existing encrypted Chat group conversation. To leave a group, pass your own user ID. Leaving does not delete the conversation for the caller. When the removal rotates the conversation key, send group_key_rotation_data and the action signatures for the removal and the key change, in that order.

put.summary: Turn On Disappearing Messages in a Chat Conversation
put.description: Sets how long new messages in a 1:1 or group Chat conversation last before they disappear, for every participant. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.

post.description: Sends a message or reaction to a Chat conversation, which you can find with `participant_query` on Get Chat Conversations. Send it end-to-end encrypted by default: `encoded_message_create_event`, built with the Chat XDK. Plaintext `content` is only a fallback for a 1:1 chat that X Chat can't encrypt: use it only when the recipient's `receives_your_chat` user field (`user.fields=receives_your_chat`) is `unencrypted`. When `content` is refused, nothing is sent and the problem's `detail` says why; HTTP 400 https://api.x.com/2/problems/encryption-required means the chat can be encrypted or is a group, so send it encrypted instead. A recipient you can't message (closed inbox, system account, or a block) returns HTTP 403 https://api.x.com/2/problems/recipient-not-messageable.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A conversation's id from Get Chat Conversations, or the recipient's user ID for a 1:1 chat.

post.description: Deletes one or more messages from a Chat conversation. Delete for all removes a message you sent (or, in groups you administer, any message) for every participant; delete for self removes any message only from your own view.

delete.description: Unmutes notifications for a Chat conversation for the authenticated user only. Works for group and 1:1 conversations. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.

post.description: Mutes notifications for a Chat conversation for the authenticated user only. Works for group and 1:1 conversations. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.

For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation: a group ID starting with `g`, the other user's ID for a 1:1 conversation, or both user IDs of a 1:1 conversation joined by a hyphen.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.

post.description: Marks a specific Chat conversation as read on behalf of the authenticated user. Without action_signatures the conversation is marked read up to its newest event and the read receipt is unsigned. With one action signature over a MarkConversationReadEvent, the server sends that signed read receipt, marking the conversation read up to the event it names.

For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.
